name: Dicks & Fontanillis Lakes
area: Desolation Wilderness (Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit)
why: Two granite lakes under Dicks Peak next to Velma, with a Dicks Pass day hike for views over Lake Tahoe.

name: Lake Schmidell
why: Desolation's wildest corner of glacier-polished granite, with day hikes to Lakes Lois and Doris.

name: Island Lake
why: Granite-slab lake full of small islands under the Crystal Range.

name: Lake of the Woods / Ropi Lake
area: Desolation Wilderness (Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit)
why: Base for climbing Pyramid Peak, Desolation's highest point.

name: Round Top Lake
why: Volcanic Round Top and The Sisters with famous wildflowers.

name: Raymond Lake
trailhead: Pacific Crest Trail at Ebbetts Pass
why: Little-known lake under the spires of Raymond Peak.

name: Peeler Lake
why: Deep-blue lake on the Sierra crest at the Yosemite boundary with excellent fishing.

name: Crown Lake
why: Walled in by Crown Point, with day hikes to Snow Lake and Rock Island Pass.

name: Kennedy Lake
why: Huge volcanic cliffs of Kennedy and Leavitt Peaks with few people.

name: Deer Lake
why: Classic granite-slab lake country with day trips to Wire and Buck Lakes plus fishing.

name: Ten Lakes Basin
why: Basin perched above the Grand Canyon of the Tuolumne, reached over a panoramic pass.

name: Vogelsang (Fletcher/Vogelsang Lakes)
why: Lakes above 10,000 ft with day hikes to Vogelsang Pass and Evelyn Lake.

name: May Lake
why: Short hike with a Mt. Hoffmann climb for views over the whole park.

name: Lake Vernon
why: Huge granite slabs, passing Wapama Falls on the way.

name: Ostrander Lake
why: Granite bowl with a stone ski hut and Horse Ridge views to Half Dome.

name: Minaret Lake
why: The Minarets tower right behind the lake, with off-trail day trips to Cecile and Iceberg Lakes.

name: Iceberg Lake
why: Lake under Clyde Minaret's sheer wall.

name: Gem Lake
why: Turquoise dammed lake with an old tram line along the trail.

name: Lillian Lake
why: Quiet west-side granite lakes with Chain Lakes day hikes.

name: Deer Lakes
why: High ridge walk along the volcanic Mammoth Crest with Ritter Range views.

name: Pioneer Basin
why: Big lake basin under Mts. Stanford, Crocker, Hopkins and Huntington.

name: Fourth Recess Lake
why: Waterfall-fed lake inside a cliff-walled side canyon.

name: Big McGee / Steelhead Lakes
why: Red-, white- and purple-banded peaks with a McGee Pass day hike.

name: Lake Dorothy
why: Wild canyon geology with off-trail day trips to Bighorn Lake and Lake Wit-So-Nah-Pah.

name: Honeymoon / Upper Pine Lake
why: Cliff-hemmed, waterfall-fed lake with few visitors and an Italy Pass day hike.

name: Humphreys Basin
why: Wide granite plateau full of lakes under Mt. Humphreys, with golden trout.

name: Treasure Lakes
why: Glacial bowl under Mt. Johnson with a Bishop Pass day hike.

name: Finger / Brainard Lakes
why: Turquoise glacial lakes under Middle Palisade.

name: Fifth / Black Lakes
why: Temple Crag views and a day hike to Palisade Glacier.

name: Graveyard Lakes
why: Remote west-side granite basin.

name: Upper Morgan Lake
why: 11,100-ft lake just past Little Lakes Valley.

name: Dusy Basin
trailhead: South Lake via Bishop Pass (Inyo permit)
why: Bare granite basin with high lakes and towering peaks.

name: Charlotte Lake
why: Beyond the Kearsarge Lakes with Charlotte Dome as the backdrop.

name: Franklin Lakes
why: Rainbow-colored rock with a Franklin Pass day hike.

name: Monarch Lakes
why: Under Sawtooth Peak, with a Sawtooth Pass view NPS calls one of the grandest in the southern Sierra.

name: Crystal Lake
why: Steep climb to a dammed alpine lake with views over the valley.

name: Twin Lakes
why: Lakes under Silliman Crest.

name: Jennie Lake
why: Granite cirque with no permit needed if you stay inside the wilderness.

name: Chicken Spring Lake
why: At about 11,250 ft, the closest match to the well-loved Cottonwood Lakes.

name: Maggie Lakes
why: Rarely visited west-side lakes with golden trout.
